{\n                assertEquals(HttpStatusCode.OK, status)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Does delay and ensures that the [GMTDate] measurements report at least\n     * the specified number of [milliseconds].\n     * The reason why it's not the same is that on some platforms time granularity of GMTDate\n     * is not that high and could be even larger than a millisecond.\n     */\n    private suspend fun delayGMTDate(milliseconds: Long) {\n        var delayValue = milliseconds\n\n        do {\n            val start = GMTDate()\n            delay(delayValue)\n            val end = GMTDate()\n            if (end > start + milliseconds) {\n                break\n            }\n            if (delayValue != 1L) {\n                delayValue = 1L\n            }\n        } while (true)\n {"path":"ktor-client/ktor-client-plugins/ktor-client-call-id/common/src/io/ktor/client/plugins/callid/CallId.kt","prefix":"/*\n * Copyright 2014-2023 JetBrains s.r.o and contributors. Use of this source code is governed by the Apache 2.0 license.\n */\n\npackage io.ktor.client.plugins.callid\n\nimport io.ktor.callid.*\nimport io.ktor.client.plugins.api.*\nimport io.ktor.client.request.*\nimport io.ktor.http.*\nimport kotlin.coroutines.*\n\ninternal typealias CallIdGenerator = suspend (HttpRequestBuilder) -> String?\ninternal typealias CallIdInterceptor = (request: HttpRequestBuilder, callId: String) -> Unit\n\n/**\n * A configuration for [CallId] plugin.\n */\npublic class CallIdConfig {\n\n    internal val generators = mutableListOf<CallIdGenerator>()\n    internal val requestInterceptors = mutableListOf<CallIdInterceptor>()\n\n    /**\n     * If set to `true`, adds a default generator that uses current [CoroutineContext] to retrieve a call ID.\n     *\n     * @see withCallId\n     * @see KtorCallIdContextElement\n     */\n    public var useCoroutineContext: Boolean = true\n\n    /**\n     * Allows you to generate a call ID for an outgoing request.\n     * Generates `null` if it is impossible to generate a call ID for some reason.\n     * You can add multiple generators, and the first non-null value will be used.\n     */\n    public fun generate(block: suspend (HttpRequestBuilder) -> String?) {\n        generators.add(block)\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Allows you to add a call ID to the request.\n     *\n     * @see [addToHeader]\n     */\n    public fun intercept(block: CallIdInterceptor) {\n        requestInterceptors.add(block)\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Adds a call ID to specified header named [header].\n     *\n     * @see [intercept]\n     */\n    public fun addToHeader(header: String = HttpHeaders.XRequestId) {\n        intercept { request, callId -> request.header(header, callId) }\n    }\n}\n\n/**\n * A plugin that allows you to trace client requests end-to-end by using unique request IDs or call IDs.\n * Typically, working with a call ID in the Ktor client might look as follows:\n * 1. }\n\n        when (principal) {\n            null -> {\n                val cause = when (credentials) {\n                    null -> AuthenticationFailedCause.NoCredentials\n                    else and 1024-bits key strength.\n * Only localhost and 127.0.0.1 domains are valid with the certificate.\n */\npublic fun generateCertificate(\n    file: File? = null,\n    algorithm: String = \"SHA1withRSA\",\n    keyAlias: String = \"mykey\",\n    keyPassword: String = \"changeit\",\n    jksPassword: String = keyPassword,\n    keySizeInBits: Int = 1024,\n    keyType: KeyType = HashAlgorithm.valueOf(hashName)\n            this.sign = SignatureAlgorithm.valueOf(signName)\n            this.password = keyPassword\n            this.keySizeInBits = keySizeInBits\n            this.keyType = keyType\n            this.subject = if (keyType == KeyType.CA) DEFAULT_CA_PRINCIPAL else DEFAULT_PRINCIPAL\n            this.domains = listOf(\"127.0.0.1\", \"localhost\")\n        }\n    }\n\n    // for backwards-compatibility, we also register the certificate under this Cert-suffixed alias\n    keyStore.setCertificateEntry(keyAlias + \"Cert\", keyStore.getCertificate(keyAlias))\n\n [signerKeyPair].\n *\n * The certified key and the signer keys should all be compatible with the given [algorithm], which must be specified\n * as one of the standard names in the\n * [Signature section](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/specs/security/standard-names.html#signature-algorithms)\n * of the Java Security Standard Algorithm Names Specification.\n *\n * The generated localhost/127.0.0.1.\n *\n * The [keyType] determines the extensions that should be written in the certificate, such as [OID.ExtKeyUsage] or\n * [OID.BasicConstraints] to use the key as CA.\n */\ninternal fun generateX509Certificate(\n    subject: X500Principal,\n    issuer: X500Principal,\n    publicKey: PublicKey,\n    signerKeyPair: KeyPair,\n    algorithm: String,\n    validityDuration: Duration = 3.days,\n    keyType: KeyType = KeyType.Server,\n    domains: List<String> = listOf(\"127.0.0.1\", \"localhost\"),\n    ipAddresses: List<InetAddress> = {"path":"ktor-utils/common/src/io/ktor/util/date/GMTDateParser.kt","prefix":"/*\n* Copyright 2014-2021 JetBrains s.r.o and contributors. Use of this source code is governed by the Apache 2.0 license.\n*/\n\npackage io.ktor.util.date\n\n/**\n * Build [GMTDate] parser using [pattern] string.\n *\n * Pattern string format:\n * | Unit     | pattern char | Description                                          |\n * | -------- | ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------- |\n * | Seconds  | s            | parse seconds 0 to 60                                |\n * | Minutes  | m            | parse minutes 0 to 60                                |\n * | Hours    | h            | parse hours 0 to 23                                  |\n * | Month    | M            | parse month from Jan to Dec(see [Month] for details) |\n * | Year     | Y            | parse year                                           |\n * | Any char | *            | Match any character                                  |\n */\npublic class GMTDateParser(private val pattern: String) {\n    init {\n        check(pattern.isNotEmpty()) { \"Date parser pattern shouldn't be empty.\" }\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Parse [GMTDate] from [dateString] using [pattern].\n     */\n    public fun parse(dateString: String): GMTDate {\n        val builder = GMTDateBuilder()\n\n        var start = 0\n        var current = pattern[start]\n        var chunkStart = 0\n        var index = 1\n\n        try {\n            while (index < pattern.length) {\n                if (pattern[index] == current) {\n                    index++\n                    continue\n                }\n\n                val chunkEnd = chunkStart + index - start\n                builder.handleToken(current, dateString.substring(chunkStart, chunkEnd))\n\n                chunkStart = chunkEnd\n                start = index\n                current = pattern[index]\n\n                index++\n            }\n\n            if (chunkStart < dateString.length) {\n                builder.handleToken(current, dateString.substring(chunkStart))\n            }\n        } catch (_: Throwable) {\n            throw InvalidDateStringException(dateString, chunkStart, pattern)\n        }\n\n        return builder.build()\n    }\n\n    private fun V : Any, out R>(\n    val calc: suspend (K) -> V,\n    val wrapFunction: (K, V, ReferenceQueue<V>) -> R\n) : Cache<K, V> where R : Reference<V>, R : CacheReference<K> {\n    private val queue = return false\n    }\n\n    override fun invalidateAll() {\n        container.invalidateAll()\n    }\n\n    private fun forkThreadIfNeeded() {\n        if (!workerThread.isAlive) {\n            throw {"path":"ktor-client/ktor-client-darwin-legacy/darwin/src/io/ktor/client/engine/darwin/certificates/LegacyCertificatePinner.kt","prefix":"/*\n* Copyright 2014-2021 JetBrains s.r.o and contributors. Use of this source code is governed by the Apache 2.0 license.\n*/\n\npackage io.ktor.client.engine.darwin.certificates\n\nimport io.ktor.client.engine.darwin.*\nimport io.ktor.client.engine.darwin.internal.legacy.*\nimport kotlinx.cinterop.*\nimport platform.CoreCrypto.*\nimport platform.CoreFoundation.*\nimport platform.Foundation.*\nimport platform.Security.*\n\n/**\n * Constrains which certificates are trusted. Pinning certificates defends against attacks on\n * certificate authorities. It also prevents connections through man-in-the-middle certificate\n * authorities either known or unknown to the application's user.\n * This class currently pins a certificate's Subject Public Key Info as described on\n * [Adam Langley's Weblog](http://goo.gl/AIx3e5). Pins are either base64 SHA-256 hashes as in\n * [HTTP Public Key Pinning (HPKP)](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7469) or SHA-1 base64 hashes as\n * in Chromium's [static certificates](http://goo.gl/XDh6je).\n *\n * ## Setting up Certificate Pinning\n *\n * The easiest way to pin a host is to turn on pinning with a broken configuration and read the\n * expected configuration when the connection fails. Be sure to do this on a trusted network, and\n * without man-in-the-middle tools like [Charles](http://charlesproxy.com) or\n * [Fiddler](http://fiddlertool.com).\n *\n * For example, to pin `https://publicobject.com`, start with a broken configuration:\n *\n * ```\n * HttpClient(Darwin) {\n *\n *     // ...\n *\n *     engine {\n *         val builder = CertificatePinner.Builder()\n *             .add(\"publicobject.com\", \"sha256/AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA=\")\n *         handleChallenge(builder.build())\n *     }\n * }\n * ```\n *\n * As expected, this fails with an exception, see the logs:\n *\n * ```\n * HttpClient: Certificate pinning failure!\n *   Peer certificate chain:\n *     sha256/afwiKY3RxoMmLkuRW1l7QsPZTJPwDS2pdDROQjXw8ig=: publicobject.com\n *     sha256/klO23nT2ehFDXCfx3eHTDRESMz3asj1muO+4aIdjiuY=: COMODO RSA Secure Server CA\n *     sha256/grX4Ta9HpZx6tSHkmCrvpApTQGo67CYDnvprLg5yRME=: COMODO RSA Certification Authority\n *     sha256/lCppFqbkrlJ3EcVFAkeip0+44VaoJUymbnOaEUk7tEU=: AddTrust External CA Root\n *   Pinned certificates for publicobject.com:\n *     sha256/AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA=\n * ```\n *\n * Follow up by pasting the public key hashes from the logs into the\n * certificate pinner's configuration:\n *\n * ```\n * val builder = CertificatePinner.Builder()\n *     .add(\"publicobject.com\", \"sha256/afwiKY3RxoMmLkuRW1l7QsPZTJPwDS2pdDROQjXw8ig=\")\n *     .add(\"publicobject.com\", \"sha256/klO23nT2ehFDXCfx3eHTDRESMz3asj1muO+4aIdjiuY=\")\n *     .add(\"publicobject.com\", \"sha256/grX4Ta9HpZx6tSHkmCrvpApTQGo67CYDnvprLg5yRME=\")\n *     .add(\"publicobject.com\", \"sha256/lCppFqbkrlJ3EcVFAkeip0+44VaoJUymbnOaEUk7tEU=\")\n * handleChallenge(builder.build())\n * ```\n *\n * ## Domain Patterns\n *\n * Pinning is per-hostname and/or per-wildcard pattern. To pin both `publicobject.com` and\n * `www.publicobject.com` you must configure both hostnames. Or you may use patterns to match\n * sets of related domain names. The following forms are permitted:\n *\n *  * **Full domain name**: you may pin an exact domain name like `www.publicobject.com`. It won't\n *    match additional prefixes (`us-west.www.publicobject.com`) or suffixes (`publicobject.com`).\n *\n *  * **Any number of subdomains**: Use two asterisks to like `**.publicobject.com` to match any\n *    number of prefixes (`us-west.www.publicobject.com`, `www.publicobject.com`) including no\n *    prefix at all (`publicobject.com`). For most applications this is the best way to configure\n *    certificate pinning.\n *\n *  * **Exactly one subdomain**: Use a single asterisk like `*.publicobject.com` to match exactly\n *    one prefix (`www.publicobject.com`, `api.publicobject.com`). Be careful with this approach as\n *    no pinning will be enforced if additional prefixes are present, or if no prefixes are present.\n *\n * Note that any other form is unsupported. You may not use asterisks in any position other than\n * the leftmost label.\n *\n * If multiple patterns match a hostname, any match is sufficient. For example, suppose pin A\n * applies to `*.publicobject.com` and pin B applies to `api.publicobject.com`. Handshakes for\n * `api.publicobject.com` are valid if either A's or B's certificate is in the chain.\n *\n * ## Warning: Certificate Pinning is Dangerous!\n *\n * Pinning certificates limits your server team's abilities to update their TLS certificates. By\n * pinning certificates, you take on additional operational complexity and limit your ability to\n * migrate between certificate authorities. Do not use certificate pinning without the blessing of\n * your server's TLS administrator!\n *\n * See also [OWASP: Certificate and Public Key Pinning](https://www.owasp.org/index\n * .php/Certificate_and_Public_Key_Pinning).\n *\n * This class was heavily inspired by OkHttp, which is a great Http library for Android\n * It provides only quiescent consistency for its operations.*\n *\n * In particular, the following execution is permitted for this queue, but is not permitted for a linearizable queue:\n *\n * ```\n * Thread 1: addLast(1) = true, removeFirstOrNull() = null\n * Thread 2: addLast(2) = 2 // this operation is concurrent with both operations in the first thread\n * ```\n */\ninternal class LockFreeMPSCQueue<E : Any> {\n    private val _cur = atomic(Core<E>(Core.INITIAL_CAPACITY))\n\n    // Note: it is not atomic w.r.t. remove operation (remove can transiently fail when isEmpty is false)\n    val isEmpty: Boolean get() = _cur.value.isEmpty\n\n    fun close() {\n        _cur.loop { cur ->\n            if (cur.close()) return // closed this copy\n            _cur.compareAndSet(cur, cur.next()) // move to next\n        }\n    }\n\n    fun addLast(element: E): Boolean {\n        _cur.loop { cur ->\n            when (cur.addLast(element)) {\n                Core.ADD_SUCCESS -> return true\n                Core.ADD_CLOSED -> return false\n                Core.ADD_FROZEN -> _cur.compareAndSet(cur, cur.next()) // move to next\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    @Suppress(\"UNCHECKED_CAST\")\n    fun removeFirstOrNull(): E? {\n        _cur.loop { cur ->\n            val result = cur.removeFirstOrNull()\n            if (result !== Core.REMOVE_FROZEN) return result as E?\n            _cur.compareAndSet(cur, cur.next())\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/**\n * Lock-free Multiply-Producer Single-Consumer Queue core.\n * *Note: This queue is NOT linearizable. plugin that provides the capability to compress a response and decompress request bodies.\n * You can use different compression algorithms, including `gzip` and `deflate`,\n * specify the required conditions for compressing data (such as a content type or response size),\n * or even compress data based on specific request parameters.\n *\n * Note that if the request body was decompressed,\n * can be accessed through [ApplicationRequest.appliedDecoders] property.\n *\n * The example below shows how to compress JavaScript content using `gzip` with the specified priority:\n * ```kotlin\n * }\n}\n\n@OptIn(InternalAPI::class)\nprivate fun decode(call: PipelineCall, options: CompressionOptions) {\n    val encodingRaw = call.request.headers[HttpHeaders.ContentEncoding]\n    if (encodingRaw        return\n    }\n    val encoderNames = encoders.map { it.encoder.name }\n    if (encoding.size > encoders.size) {\n        val missingEncoders = encoding.map { it.value } - {"path":"ktor-client/ktor-client-darwin/darwin/src/io/ktor/client/engine/darwin/certificates/CertificatePinner.kt","prefix":"/*\n* Copyright 2014-2021 JetBrains s.r.o and contributors. Use of this source code is governed by the Apache 2.0 license.\n*/\n\npackage io.ktor.client.engine.darwin.certificates\n\nimport io.ktor.client.engine.darwin.*\nimport kotlinx.cinterop.*\nimport platform.CoreCrypto.*\nimport platform.CoreFoundation.*\nimport platform.Foundation.*\nimport platform.Security.*\n\n/**\n * Constrains which certificates are trusted. Pinning certificates defends against attacks on\n * certificate authorities. It also prevents connections through man-in-the-middle certificate\n * authorities either known or unknown to the application's user.\n * This class currently pins a certificate's Subject Public Key Info as described on\n * [Adam Langley's Weblog](http://goo.gl/AIx3e5). Pins are either base64 SHA-256 hashes as in\n * [HTTP Public Key Pinning (HPKP)](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7469) or SHA-1 base64 hashes as\n * in Chromium's [static certificates](http://goo.gl/XDh6je).\n *\n * ## Setting up Certificate Pinning\n *\n * The easiest way to pin a host is to turn on pinning with a broken configuration and read the\n * expected configuration when the connection fails. Be sure to do this on a trusted network, and\n * without man-in-the-middle tools like [Charles](http://charlesproxy.com) or\n * [Fiddler](http://fiddlertool.com).\n *\n * For example, to pin `https://publicobject.com`, start with a broken configuration:\n *\n * ```\n * HttpClient(Darwin) {\n *\n *     // ...\n *\n *     engine {\n *         val builder = CertificatePinner.Builder()\n *             .add(\"publicobject.com\", \"sha256/AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA=\")\n *         handleChallenge(builder.build())\n *     }\n * }\n * ```\n *\n * As expected, this fails with an exception, see the logs:\n *\n * ```\n * HttpClient: Certificate pinning failure!\n *   Peer certificate chain:\n *     sha256/afwiKY3RxoMmLkuRW1l7QsPZTJPwDS2pdDROQjXw8ig=: publicobject.com\n *     sha256/klO23nT2ehFDXCfx3eHTDRESMz3asj1muO+4aIdjiuY=: COMODO RSA Secure Server CA\n *     sha256/grX4Ta9HpZx6tSHkmCrvpApTQGo67CYDnvprLg5yRME=: COMODO RSA Certification Authority\n *     sha256/lCppFqbkrlJ3EcVFAkeip0+44VaoJUymbnOaEUk7tEU=: AddTrust External CA Root\n *   Pinned certificates for publicobject.com:\n *     sha256/AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA=\n * ```\n *\n * Follow up by pasting the public key hashes from the logs into the\n * certificate pinner's configuration:\n *\n * ```\n * val builder = CertificatePinner.Builder()\n *     .add(\"publicobject.com\", \"sha256/afwiKY3RxoMmLkuRW1l7QsPZTJPwDS2pdDROQjXw8ig=\")\n *     .add(\"publicobject.com\", \"sha256/klO23nT2ehFDXCfx3eHTDRESMz3asj1muO+4aIdjiuY=\")\n *     .add(\"publicobject.com\", \"sha256/grX4Ta9HpZx6tSHkmCrvpApTQGo67CYDnvprLg5yRME=\")\n *     .add(\"publicobject.com\", \"sha256/lCppFqbkrlJ3EcVFAkeip0+44VaoJUymbnOaEUk7tEU=\")\n * handleChallenge(builder.build())\n * ```\n *\n * ## Domain Patterns\n *\n * Pinning is per-hostname and/or per-wildcard pattern. To pin both `publicobject.com` and\n * `www.publicobject.com` you must configure both hostnames. Or you may use patterns to match\n * sets of related domain names. The following forms are permitted:\n *\n *  * **Full domain name**: you may pin an exact domain name like `www.publicobject.com`. It won't\n *    match additional prefixes (`us-west.www.publicobject.com`) or suffixes (`publicobject.com`).\n *\n *  * **Any number of subdomains**: Use two asterisks to like `**.publicobject.com` to match any\n *    number of prefixes (`us-west.www.publicobject.com`, `www.publicobject.com`) including no\n *    prefix at all (`publicobject.com`). For most applications this is the best way to configure\n *    certificate pinning.\n *\n *  * **Exactly one subdomain**: Use a single asterisk like `*.publicobject.com` to match exactly\n *    one prefix (`www.publicobject.com`, `api.publicobject.com`). Be careful with this approach as\n *    no pinning will be enforced if additional prefixes are present, or if no prefixes are present.\n *\n * Note that any other form is unsupported. You may not use asterisks in any position other than\n * the leftmost label.\n *\n * If multiple patterns match a hostname, any match is sufficient. For example, suppose pin A\n * applies to `*.publicobject.com` and pin B applies to `api.publicobject.com`. Handshakes for\n * `api.publicobject.com` are valid if either A's or B's certificate is in the chain.\n *\n * ## Warning: Certificate Pinning is Dangerous!\n *\n * Pinning certificates limits your server team's abilities to update their TLS certificates. By\n * pinning certificates, you take on additional operational complexity and limit your ability to\n * migrate between certificate authorities. Do not use certificate pinning without the blessing of\n * your server's TLS administrator!\n *\n * See also [OWASP: Certificate and Public Key Pinning](https://www.owasp.org/index\n * .php/Certificate_and_Public_Key_Pinning).\n *\n * This class was heavily inspired by OkHttp, which is a great Http library for Android\n * {"path":"ktor-utils/jvm/src/io/ktor/util/cio/FileChannels.kt","prefix":"/*\n * Copyright 2014-2019 JetBrains s.r.o and contributors. io.ktor.utils.io.jvm.nio.*\nimport kotlinx.coroutines.*\nimport java.io.*\nimport java.nio.channels.*\nimport kotlin.coroutines.*\n\n/**\n * Launch a coroutine to open a read channel for a file and fill it.\n * Please note that file reading is blocking so if you are starting it on [Dispatchers.Unconfined] it may block\n * your async code and freeze the whole application when runs on a pool that is not intended for blocking operations.\n * This is why [coroutineContext] should have [Dispatchers.IO] or\n * a coroutine dispatcher that is properly configured for blocking IO.\n */\npublic fun File.readChannel(\n    start: Long = 0,\n    endInclusive: Long = ","middle":"-1,\n","suffix":"    coroutineContext: CoroutineContext = Dispatchers.IO\n): ByteReadChannel {\n    val fileLength = length()\n    val randomAccessFile by lazy { RandomAccessFile(this@readChannel, \"r\") }\n    val writer = CoroutineScope(coroutineContext).writer(\n        CoroutineName(\"file-reader\") + coroutineContext,\n        autoFlush = false\n    ) {\n        require(start >= 0L) { \"start position shouldn't be negative but it is $start\" }\n        require(endInclusive <= fileLength - 1) {\n            \"endInclusive points to the position out of the file: file size = $fileLength, endInclusive = $endInclusive\"\n        }\n\n        @Suppress(\"BlockingMethodInNonBlockingContext\")\n    nioChannel: WritableByteChannel,\n    selectable: Selectable,\n    selector: SelectorManager,\n    socketOptions: SocketOptions.TCPClientSocketOptions? = null\n): ReaderJob = reader(Dispatchers.IO        public const val qualityQueryParameter: Double = 1.0\n\n        /**\n         * Quality of [RouteSelectorEvaluation] when a parameter with prefix or suffix is matched.\n         */\n         */\n        public const val qualityParameter: Double = 0.8\n\n        /**\n         * Quality of [RouteSelectorEvaluation] when a path parameter is matched.\n         */\n        public const @Suppress(\"unused\")\n        public const val qualityMethodParameter: Double = qualityParameter\n\n        /**\n         * Quality of [RouteSelectorEvaluation] when a wildcard is matched.\n         */\n        public const val qualityWildcard: Double = 0.5\n\n        /**\n         * Quality of [RouteSelectorEvaluation] when an optional parameter is missing.\n         */\n        public const val RootRouteSelector(rootPath: String = \"\") : RouteSelector() {\n\n    private val parts = RoutingPath.parse(rootPath).parts.map {\n        require(it.kind == RoutingPathSegmentKind.Constant) {\n            \"rootPath should be constant, no wildcards supported.\"\n        }\n        it.value\n    }\n\n    private val successEvaluationResult = RouteSelectorEvaluation.Success(\n        RouteSelectorEvaluation.qualityConstant,\n        segmentIncrement = parts.size\n    )\n\n    override suspend fun evaluate(context: RoutingResolveContext, segmentIndex: Int): RouteSelectorEvaluation {\n        check(segmentIndex == 0) { \"Root selector should be evaluated first.\" }\n        if (parts.isEmpty()) {\n            return RouteSelectorEvaluation.Constant\n        }\n\n        val parts = parts\n        val segments = context.segments\n        if (segments.size < parts.size) {\n            return RouteSelectorEvaluation.FailedPath\n        }\n\n        for (index in segmentIndex until segmentIndex + parts.size) {\n            if (segments[index] != parts[index]) {\n                return RouteSelectorEvaluation.FailedPath\n            }\n        }\n\n        return successEvaluationResult\n    }\n\n    override fun toString(): String = parts.joinToString(\"/\")\n}\n\n/**\n * Evaluates a route against a constant query parameter value.\n * @param name is a {"path":"ktor-server/ktor-server-plugins/ktor-server-auth/common/src/io/ktor/server/auth/BasicAuth.kt","prefix":"/*\n* Copyright 2014-2021 JetBrains s.r.o and contributors. Use of this source code is governed by the Apache 2.0 license.\n*/\n\npackage io.ktor.server.auth\n\nimport io.ktor.http.auth.*\nimport io.ktor.server.application.*\nimport io.ktor.server.request.*\nimport io.ktor.server.response.*\nimport io.ktor.util.*\nimport io.ktor.utils.io.charsets.*\n\n/**\n * A `basic` [Authentication] provider.\n *\n * @see [basic]\n * @property name is the name of the provider, or `null` for a default provider.\n */\npublic class BasicAuthenticationProvider internal constructor(\n    config: Config\n) : AuthenticationProvider(config) {\n    internal val realm: String = config.realm\n\n    internal val charset: Charset? = config.charset\n\n    internal val authenticationFunction = config.authenticationFunction\n\n    override suspend fun onAuthenticate(context: AuthenticationContext) {\n        val call = context.call\n        val credentials = call.request.basicAuthenticationCredentials(charset)\n        val principal = credentials?.let { authenticationFunction(call, it) }\n\n        val cause = when {\n            credentials == null -> AuthenticationFailedCause.NoCredentials\n            principal == null -> AuthenticationFailedCause.InvalidCredentials\n            else -> null\n        }\n\n        if (cause != null) {\n            @Suppress(\"NAME_SHADOWING\")\n            context.challenge(basicAuthenticationChallengeKey, cause) { challenge, call ->\n                call.respond(UnauthorizedResponse(HttpAuthHeader.basicAuthChallenge(realm, charset)))\n                challenge.complete()\n            }\n        }\n        if (principal != null) {\n            context.principal(name, principal)\n        }\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * A configuration for the [basic] authentication provider.\n     */\n    public class Config internal constructor(name: String?) : AuthenticationProvider.Config(name) {\n        internal var authenticationFunction: AuthenticationFunction<UserPasswordCredential> = {\n            throw NotImplementedError(\n                \"Basic auth validate function is not specified. Otherwise, this implementation will produce\n * `StackOverflowError`.\n *\n * @suppress **This is unstable API and it is subject to change.**\n */\npublic abstract class AtomicOp<in T> : OpDescriptor() {\n    private val _consensus = atomic<Any?>(NO_DECISION)\n\n    public val isDecided: Boolean get() = _consensus.value !== NO_DECISION\n\n    public fun tryDecide(decision: Any?): Boolean {\n        check(decision !== NO_DECISION)\n        return _consensus.compareAndSet(NO_DECISION, decision)\n    }\n\n    private fun decide(decision: Any?): Any? = if (tryDecide(decision)) decision else _consensus.value\n\n    public abstract fun prepare(affected: T): Any? // `null` if Ok, or failure reason\n\n    public abstract fun complete(affected: T, failure: Any?) // failure != null if failed to prepare op\n\n    // returns `null` on success\n    @Suppress(\"UNCHECKED_CAST\")\n    public final override fun perform(affected: Any?): Any? {\n        // make decision on status\n        var decision = this._consensus.value\n        if (decision === NO_DECISION) {\n            decision = decide(prepare(affected as T))\n        }\n\n        complete(affected as T, decision)\n        return decision\n    }\n}\n\n/**\n * A part of multi-step atomic operation [AtomicOp].\n *\n * @suppress **This is unstable API and it is subject to change.**\n */\npublic abstract class AtomicDesc {\n\n    // returns `null` if prepared successfully\n    public abstract fun prepare(op: AtomicOp<*>): Any?\n\n    // decision == null if success\n    public abstract fun complete(op: AtomicOp<*>, failure: Any?)\n}\n\n/**\n * Doubly-linked concurrent list node with remove support.\n * Based on paper\n * [\"Lock-Free and Practical Doubly Linked List-Based Deques Using Single-Word Compare-and-Swap\"](http://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/viewdoc/download?doi=10.1.1.140.4693&rep=rep1&type=pdf)\n * by Sundell and Tsigas.\n *\n * Important notes:\n * * The instance of this class serves both as list head/tail sentinel and as the list item.\n *   Sentinel node should be never removed.\n * * There are no operations to add items to left side of the list, only to the end (right side), because we cannot\n *   efficiently linearize them with atomic multi-step head-removal operations. Returns prev non-removed Node\n    public val prevNode: Node get() = prev.unwrap()\n\n    // ------ addOneIfEmpty ------\n\n    public fun addOneIfEmpty(node: Node): Boolean {\n        node._prev.lazySet(this)\n        node._next.lazySet(this)\n        while (true) {\n            val next = next\n            if (next !== this) return false // this is not an empty list!\n            if (_next.compareAndSet(this, node)) {\n                // added successfully (linearized add) -- fixup the list\n                node.finishAdd(this)\n                return true\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ------ addLastXXX ------\n\n    /**\n     * Adds last item to this list.\n     */\n    public fun addLast(node: Node) {\n        while (true) { // lock-free loop on prev.next\n // sentinel node is never removed, so prev is always defined\n            when (prev.tryCondAddNext(node, this, condAdd)) {\n                SUCCESS -> return true\n                FAILURE -> return false\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    public inline fun addLastIfPrev(node: Node, predicate: (Node) -> Boolean): Boolean {\n        while (true) { // lock-free loop on prev.next\n            val prev = prev as Node // sentinel node is never removed, so prev is always defined\n            if (!predicate(prev)) return false\n            if (prev.addNext(node, this)) return true\n        }\n clock()\n                    if (remaining <= 0 && isStarted.value) {\n                        break\n                    }\n\n                    delay(remaining)\n                }\n                yield()\n                onTimeout()\n            } catch (cause: Throwable) {\n                // no op\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/**\n * Starts timeout coroutine that will invoke [onTimeout] after [timeoutMs] of inactivity.\n * Use [Timeout] object to wrap code that can timeout or cancel this coroutine\n */\ninternal fun CoroutineScope.createTimeout(\n    name: String = \"\",\n    timeoutMs: Long,\n    clock: () -> Long = { getTimeMillis() },\n    onTimeout: suspend () -> Unit\n): Timeout {\n    return Timeout(name, timeoutMs, clock, this, onTimeout)\n}\n\ninternal inline fun <T> Timeout?.withTimeout(block: () -> T): T {\n    if (this == null) {\n        return block()\n    }\n\n    start()\n    return try {\n        block()\n    } finally {\n        stop()\n    }\n}\n","contexts":[{"path":"ktor-network/jvm/src/io/ktor/network/util/Pools.kt","content":"internal const val DEFAULT_BYTE_BUFFER_POOL_SIZE: Int = 4096\ninternal const val DEFAULT_BYTE_BUFFER_BUFFER_SIZE: Int = 4096\npublic val DefaultByteBufferPool: ObjectPool<ByteBuffer> =\n    DirectByteBufferPool(DEFAULT_BYTE_BUFFER_POOL_SIZE, DEFAULT_BYTE_BUFFER_BUFFER_SIZE)\npublic val DefaultDatagramByteBufferPool: ObjectPool<ByteBuffer> =\n    DirectByteBufferPool(2048, MAX_DATAGRAM_SIZE)","language":"Kotlin","origin":"PackageDeclarations","picker":"All"}],"code-engine":{"type":"TOKEN_MIDDLE","language":"Kotlin","ce-version":"0.3.119","duration-ms":0}}

kotlin.coroutines.*\n\n/**\n * Event loop dispatcher","middle":" having a queue of the specified [queueSize].\n * Unlike a plain queue-based event dispatcher, this one does resume input interest on dispatch.\n */\ninternal class ReactorLoopDispatcher(\n    private val interestController: InterestControllerHolder,\n    private val queueSize: Int\n) : CoroutineDispatcher() {\n    private val queue = ArrayBlockingQueue<Runnable>(queueSize)\n\n    override fun dispatch(context: CoroutineContext, block: Runnable) {\n        if (context[Job]?.isCancelled == true) {\n            // we can't just enqueue this because it is likely we'll have no chance to process the loop\n            // so we execute it immediately\n            // this is safe because we know what the job is running on this dispatcher\n            // and it will simply exit in case of cancellation\n            // so running block.run will just complete the job and invoke all completion handlers\n            // that is safe in this particular case.\n            block.run()\n        } else {\n            check(queue.add(block)) { \"Dispatcher queue of size $queueSize is full: $queue\" }\n            interestController.resumeInputIfPossible()\n        }\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * This should be only invoked from a reactor thread.\n     */\n    fun processLoop() {\n        while (true) {\n            queue.poll()?.run() ?: break\n        }\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Check if there are queued tasks.\n     */\n    fun hasTasks(): Boolean = In debug mode users will get more details in the stacktrace.\n     */\n    public open val developmentMode: Boolean = false\n\n    private val phasesRaw: MutableList<Any> = mutableListOf(*phases)\n\n    private var interceptorsQuantity = 0\n\n    /**\n     * Phases of this pipeline\n     */\n    public val items: List<PipelinePhase>\n        get() = phasesRaw.map {\n            it as? If there are other phases inserted after [reference], then [phase]\n     * will be inserted after them.\n     * Example:\n     * ```\n     * val pipeline = Pipeline<String, String>(a)\n     * pipeline.insertPhaseAfter(a, b)\n     * pipeline.insertPhaseAfter(a, c)\n     * assertEquals(listOf(a, b, c), pipeline.items)\n     * ```\n     */\n    public fun insertPhaseAfter(reference: PipelinePhase, phase: PipelinePhase) {\n        if (hasPhase(phase)) return\n\n        val index = findPhaseIndex(reference)\n        if (index == -1) {\n            throw InvalidPhaseException(\"Phase $reference was not registered for this pipeline\")\n        }\n        // insert after the last phase that has Relation.After on [reference]\n        var lastRelatedPhaseIndex = index\n        for (i in index + 1..phasesRaw.lastIndex) {\n            val relation = (phasesRaw[i] as? PhaseContent<*, *>)?.relation ?: break\n            val relatedTo = (relation as? PipelinePhaseRelation.After)?.relativeTo ?: continue\n            lastRelatedPhaseIndex = if (relatedTo == reference) i else lastRelatedPhaseIndex\n        }\n\n        phasesRaw.add(\n PipelinePhase, block: PipelineInterceptor<TSubject, TContext>) {\n        val phaseContent = findPhase(phase)\n            ?: throw InvalidPhaseException(\"Phase $phase was not registered for this while (iterator.hasNext()) {\n                val fromPhaseOrContent = iterator.next()\n\n                val fromPhase = (fromPhaseOrContent as? PipelinePhase)\n                    ?: (fromPhaseOrContent as PhaseContent<*, *>).phase\n\n                if (hasPhase(fromPhase)) {\n                    iterator.remove()\n                } else {\n                    val inserted = insertRelativePhase(fromPhaseOrContent, fromPhase)\n                    if (inserted) {\n                        iterator.remove()\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    private fun mergeInterceptors(from: Pipeline<TSubject, TContext>) {\n        if (interceptorsQuantity == 0) {\n            setInterceptorsListFromAnotherPipeline(from)\n        } else {\n            resetInterceptorsList()\n        }\n\n        val fromPhases = from.phasesRaw\n        fromPhases.forEach { fromPhaseOrContent ->\n            val fromPhase = (fromPhaseOrContent as? PipelinePhase)\n                ?: (fromPhaseOrContent as PhaseContent<*, *>).phase\n\n            if (fromPhaseOrContent is PhaseContent<*, *> && !fromPhaseOrContent.isEmpty) {\n                @Suppress(\"UNCHECKED_CAST\")\n                fromPhaseOrContent as PhaseContent<TSubject, TContext>\n\n                fromPhaseOrContent.addTo(findPhase(fromPhase)!!)\n                interceptorsQuantity += fromPhaseOrContent.size\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Merges another pipeline into this pipeline, maintaining relative phases order\n     */\n    public fun merge(from: Pipeline<TSubject, TContext>) {\n        if (fastPathMerge(from)) {\n            return\n        }\n\n        mergePhases(from)\n        mergeInterceptors(from)\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Reset current pipeline from other.\n     */\n    public fun resetFrom(from: Pipeline<TSubject, TContext>) {\n        phasesRaw.clear()\n        check(interceptorsQuantity == 0)\n\n        fastPathMerge(from)\n    }\n\n    override fun toString(): String {\n        val interceptors = interceptorsForTests()\n            .joinToString(\"\\n\") { \"    \" + it::class.toString() }\n\n        return \"${this::class}(0x${hashCode().toString(16)}) [\\n$interceptors\\n]\"\n    }\n\n    internal fun phaseInterceptors(phase: PipelinePhase): List<PipelineInterceptor<TSubject, TContext>> =\n        findPhase(phase)?.sharedInterceptors() ?: emptyList()\n\n    /**\n     * For tests only\n     */\n    internal fun interceptorsForTests(): List<PipelineInterceptor<TSubject, TContext>> {\n        return interceptors ?: cacheInterceptors()\n    }\n\n    private fun createContext(\n        context: TContext,\n        subject: TSubject,\n        coroutineContext: CoroutineContext\n    ): PipelineContext<TSubject, TContext> =\n        pipelineContextFor(context, sharedInterceptorsList(), subject, coroutineContext, developmentMode)\n\n    private fun findPhase(phase: PipelinePhase): PhaseContent<TSubject, TContext>? PhaseContent<TSubject, TContext> ?: continue\n\n                if (phaseContent.isEmpty) continue\n\n                val interceptors = phaseContent.sharedInterceptors()\n                setInterceptorsListFromPhase(phaseContent)\n                return interceptors\n            }\n        }\n\n        val destination: MutableList<PipelineInterceptor<TSubject, TContext>> = mutableListOf()\n        for (phaseIndex in 0..phases.lastIndex) {\n            @Suppress(\"UNCHECKED_CAST\")\n            val phase = phases[phaseIndex] as?
